note: One feature per developer run, in order. Statuses: pending | done | failed. The developer edits only the entry it worked on.

features.title: Cook meat at a furnace
features.what: A person with raw meat and a furnace in reach (or one in the bag, placed) smelts it with real fuel (logs/planks/coal) and eats cooked food. When hungry and holding raw meat, prefer cooking before eating.
features.acceptance: Someone with raw beef and logs ends up with cooked beef; lastMeal shows COOKED_*.

features.title: Furnace from cobblestone
features.what: Crafting resolves FURNACE (8 cobblestone) through the existing chain so a person who mines can make one, and places it near their bench.
features.acceptance: A person with a pickaxe and no furnace acquires one without any item being handed out.

features.title: Stone tools after wooden
features.what: Once a person holds 3+ cobblestone, tool wants upgrade: STONE_PICKAXE, STONE_AXE, STONE_SWORD, STONE_HOE replace wooden ones in the craft wish list.
features.acceptance: A miner with a wooden pickaxe and cobblestone makes a stone pickaxe and holds it.

features.title: Bread from wheat
features.what: A farmer who reaps wheat bakes bread (3 wheat) at a bench and eats it; bread is preferred over raw meat when both are held.
features.acceptance: lastMeal BREAD appears for a farmer within two harvests.

features.title: Berries and apples as forage
features.what: Sweet berry bushes and apples from oak leaves count: a hungry person with no meat gathers berries/apples within 24 blocks before hunting.
features.acceptance: A hungry person near berry bushes eats SWEET_BERRIES.

features.title: Sleep at night without an inn
features.what: With no inn in reach, a person makes a one-block shelter (dig in or a 1x2 hut) and sleeps through the night; hp regen doubles while asleep.
features.acceptance: At night people stop working and 'asleep' appears in activity.

features.title: Torches against the dark
features.what: People who hold coal and sticks craft torches and place one where they work at night and one at their bed.
features.acceptance: Torches appear at camps and fields at night.

features.title: Fall damage like a player
features.what: Falls of more than 3 blocks take (blocks-3) hp; the walker refuses drops over 6 unless into water.
features.acceptance: A person never dies to a fall the walker chose.

features.title: Fire and lava are fatal hazards
features.what: The walker never paths through lava or fire; a person adjacent to lava backs away; burning takes hp.
features.acceptance: No person ever stands in lava.

features.title: Tool upkeep
features.what: A person checks tool durability and crafts a replacement before it breaks.
features.acceptance: Nobody carries a tool under 10% durability for long.

features.title: Coal and iron smelting
features.what: A miner with raw iron and a furnace smelts ingots using coal first, then planks; iron tools enter the craft wish list.
features.acceptance: An IRON_PICKAXE appears in someone's bag with no item ever handed out.

features.title: Staircase mining to ore depth
features.what: Mining digs a proper staircase down to y=16 and branch-mines, placing a torch every 8 blocks and never digging under its own feet.
features.acceptance: A miner returns with raw iron and coal; the shaft has torches.

features.title: Copper
features.what: Copper ore is mined and smelted; copper is a trade good with a base value and feeds any vanilla copper recipe present.
features.acceptance: Copper ingots appear in bags and have a base value.

features.title: Leather armour
features.what: A person with 5+ leather crafts leather armour and wears it (equipment slots); armour reduces damage taken.
features.acceptance: A person is seen wearing leather armour.

features.title: Shears and wool
features.what: Shears from 2 iron; sheep are sheared rather than killed when wool is the need, and regrow.
features.acceptance: A person with shears shears without killing.

features.title: Buckets and water
features.what: An iron bucket lets a farmer carry water to a dry field and a builder make an infinite water source.
features.acceptance: A field with no nearby water gets irrigated.

features.title: Stone bricks for walls
features.what: Builders who hold cobblestone make stone bricks and use them for inn walls when available, planks otherwise.
features.acceptance: An inn built by a stone-holding builder has stone walls.

features.title: Glass windows
features.what: Sand is smelted to glass; buildings get window panes in the wall pattern.
features.acceptance: Inns built after this have glass.

features.title: Bone meal
features.what: Bones (from lore-placed skeletons) or composted plants make bone meal; farmers use it to speed crops.
features.acceptance: Crop growth accelerates when bone meal is held.

features.title: Fishing rod from string
features.what: String from cobwebs in mineshafts or spiders when present; the fishing rod recipe resolves and fishing becomes possible.
features.acceptance: Somebody fishes and eats cod.

features.title: Shepherd
features.what: A herd job: lure 2 animals with wheat into a fenced pen near home; the pen is a place record; breeding with wheat produces young; the pen is a food source.
features.acceptance: A pen with 2+ animals exists and food is taken from it.

features.title: Woodcutter replants
features.what: After felling, a person plants a sapling of the same wood in the stump hole if held.
features.acceptance: Saplings appear where trees were cut.

features.title: Builder job for houses
features.what: Members of a village with 60+ planks build a 5x5 house for themselves on a free plot near the inn; the house is their home record.
features.acceptance: A village has houses beyond the inn.
features.notes: Done 2026-08-24, generalized: blueprint library (gadget:blueprints, scripts/blueprints.mjs) tiered by material cost; villages asks members for the best house they can afford; people builds it block by block, stakes the plot via gadget:claims, house becomes home.

features.title: Road layer
features.what: A villager with 32+ cobblestone lays a one-block path between inn, houses and fields.
features.acceptance: Paths connect village buildings.

features.title: Guard
features.what: A person with a sword and boldness >= 2 takes a patrol job at night around the village edge, attacking hostile mobs in reach.
features.acceptance: A patrolling guard kills a placed zombie.

features.title: Courier
features.what: Carries surplus food from a village store to a person who asked for it via chat (npc_do with want=FOOD).
features.acceptance: A courier delivers food to a hungry person.

features.title: Cook
features.what: A village cook takes raw meat from the store, cooks it at the inn furnace and returns it.
features.acceptance: Store contents change from raw to cooked over time.

features.title: Miner's cart
features.what: A miner with 5 iron and a chest crafts a chest minecart and rails into the shaft to haul loads.
features.acceptance: Rails appear in a shaft.

features.title: Explorer's report
features.what: Discovered ruins are shared to villagers via a fact record when the explorer returns.
features.acceptance: A known-places fact is written by an explorer.

features.title: Fisher's dock
features.what: A fisher with 20 planks builds a 1-wide dock into deep water and fishes from its end.
features.acceptance: A dock exists and a fisher stands on it.

features.title: Price memory
features.what: Each person remembers the last price paid for each item and adjusts their valuation toward it; a market that overcharges loses customers.
features.acceptance: The sheet has a prices map that changes after trades.

features.title: Bartering talk
features.what: When two people trade, the higher-CHA side proposes; a counteroffer loop of up to 3 rounds narrows the gap; the summary is logged as a fact both know.
features.acceptance: A trade fact with the haggling summary appears.

features.title: Village currency
features.what: The village mints a token (a renamed copper nugget) members accept at the market; outsiders pay in goods.
features.acceptance: A token item exists and is used in a market transaction.

features.title: Debt and favours
features.what: A person who cannot pay may owe; the creditor records the debt; debts are repaid from surplus; unpaid debts lower the creditor's regard for the debtor.
features.acceptance: A debt is recorded and later cleared.

features.title: Traveling merchant
features.what: One high-CHA trader takes a peddle job: walks between villages carrying goods from the store with the biggest surplus to the one with the biggest shortage.
features.acceptance: Goods move between two stores by a walker.

features.title: Market stall
features.what: A village with 4+ members and a store builds a stall with a sign listing the store's top goods and prices.
features.acceptance: A sign near the store lists goods.

features.title: Gifts
features.what: People with warmth give a small gift to the person nearby whose social need is lowest; the receiver's social need rises.
features.acceptance: A gift event appears.

features.title: Reputation
features.what: Each person has a reputation raised by kept promises, gifts and fair trades, lowered by theft or broken promises; reputation shades market markup.
features.acceptance: Reputation field exists and moves.

features.title: Theft
features.what: A person with low CHA, high boldness and hunger under 4 may steal from a store; if seen by a member, reputation drops and a guard responds.
features.acceptance: A theft event appears with a witness.

features.title: Wages
features.what: A village pays members from the store for completed village jobs (build, patrol, cook); wages are recorded on the sheet.
features.acceptance: A wage payment appears after a village job.

features.title: Ask for directions
features.what: Players can ask an NPC where a village, person or ruin is; the actor answers from the places ledger and looks toward it.
features.acceptance: An actor answers a where-is question with coordinates.

features.title: NPCs talk to each other
features.what: When two people spend 30+ seconds within 4 blocks, a short in-character exchange is generated once per pair per hour via the actor and spoken with npc_say; cheap model only.
features.acceptance: Two NPCs are seen speaking near each other.

features.title: Promise follow-through
features.what: When a chat-assigned job finishes, the person walks back to the asker if within 64 blocks and reports via npc_say.
features.acceptance: An NPC reports back after a chat-assigned job.

features.title: Rumours
features.what: Facts with knownBy spread: when two people meet, one fact each is shared with a probability weighted by CHA.
features.acceptance: A fact's knownBy list grows through meetings.

features.title: Greetings by name
features.what: NPCs greet players they have met before by name and remember the last thing they were asked.
features.acceptance: Actor memory shows the player's name on a second meeting.

features.title: Mood in speech
features.what: The actor prompt includes a one-line mood derived from happiness and needs so replies change tone when hungry or hurt.
features.acceptance: Replies differ between a fed and a starving NPC.

features.title: Quests from needs
features.what: An NPC with a need below 8 may ask a nearby player for help with a concrete task and records it as a quest; completing it raises reputation and the need.
features.acceptance: A quest record is created by an NPC and completed by a player.

features.title: Naming places
features.what: The founder of a village names it in conversation if asked; the name updates the place record.
features.acceptance: A village is renamed via chat.

features.title: Mourning
features.what: When a person dies, those who knew them lose social/happiness and speak of them when asked; the head's location is a fact they know.
features.acceptance: NPCs mention a dead friend by name.

features.title: Recruiting
features.what: A village member with CHA >= 2 invites lingering non-members to join; joining time halves after an invitation.
features.acceptance: A join event cites an inviter.

features.title: Sheet on sneak-click
features.what: Right-clicking an NPC while sneaking opens a chest-style GUI showing abilities, skills, needs and bag (read-only).
features.acceptance: A GUI opens for a sneaking player.

features.title: Village board
features.what: A village has a lectern with a book at the inn listing members, jobs, store contents and open quests.
features.acceptance: A book in the inn lists current facts.

features.title: Trade window
features.what: Players can open a trade GUI with an NPC: the NPC offers items at its valuation; the player pays with items.
features.acceptance: A player buys bread from an NPC in a GUI.

features.title: Name tags with status
features.what: The name above each NPC shows a small status glyph: hunger, job, village.
features.acceptance: Name tags update live.

features.title: Tab list faces
features.what: Tab entries carry the NPC's skin face and a suffix with their village.
features.acceptance: Tab list shows faces.

features.title: Console: people page
features.what: The Lore Console gets a /people page listing everyone with needs, skills, job and a click-to-locate.
features.acceptance: /people renders.

features.title: Console: village layer
features.what: The map shows village boundaries, inns, stores and fields as overlays.
features.acceptance: Overlays render on /map.

features.title: Scoreboard sidebar
features.what: Players near a village see a sidebar with its name, population and store food count.
features.acceptance: Sidebar appears near a village.

features.title: Death notices
features.what: When an NPC dies, nearby players get a chat line from someone who knew them, and the head location.
features.acceptance: A death notice appears.

features.title: Quest log command
features.what: Players can type a command to list quests NPCs have given them.
features.acceptance: A quest list prints.

features.title: Silver
features.what: A lore ore: a deepslate-level silver (a display-named raw iron variant) found by miners below y=0; a currency metal and a cheap tool tier.
features.acceptance: Silver appears in a miner's bag.

features.title: Gem finds
features.what: Rare emerald/diamond finds while mining at depth; gems are high-value trade goods the market prices by scarcity.
features.acceptance: A gem trade occurs.

features.title: Clay and bricks
features.what: Clay from riverbanks is smelted into bricks; brick buildings are the premium tier.
features.acceptance: A brick building exists.

features.title: Herbalism
features.what: An eleventh skill (leans on WIS): gathering flowers and mushrooms and brewing a simple healing tea at a campfire that restores hp.
features.acceptance: A person heals with tea.

features.title: Charms
features.what: A crafter with high INT makes a charm (a renamed item) that grants +1 to one ability while held; charms trade at high value.
features.acceptance: A charm exists and changes an aptitude.

features.title: Wards
features.what: A village with a shrine (a small built structure) halves hostile spawns within 48 blocks.
features.acceptance: A shrine exists and spawn counts drop.

features.title: Spellbooks
features.what: Rare books found in ruins teach one spell to a reader with INT >= 2: light (places torches at range), mend (repairs a tool), ward.
features.acceptance: A spell is learned and cast.

features.title: Mana
features.what: People who know a spell gain a mana meter that refills with rest; casting costs mana.
features.acceptance: Mana appears on a caster's sheet.

features.title: Enchanting
features.what: Villages with a library building and 15 bookshelves can enchant tools; enchanted tools carry real enchantments.
features.acceptance: An enchanted tool exists.

features.title: Omens
features.what: The director may place an omen (a lightning strike, a ruin appearing); NPCs who witness it gain a fact and talk about it.
features.acceptance: An omen fact spreads.

features.title: Daily plan
features.what: Each person makes a plan at dawn: three goals for the day ordered by needs and skills; jobs are chosen from the plan first.
features.acceptance: A plan field appears at dawn and is followed.

features.title: Long-term goal
features.what: Each person has one long-term goal (own a house, reach skill 5, found a village, get rich); goals shade job weights.
features.acceptance: A goal field exists and drives choices.

features.title: Stockpile targets
features.what: People keep a target count for food, logs, cobblestone and tools and work toward shortfalls.
features.acceptance: Targets appear and gathering stops at the target.

features.title: Home base
features.what: Each person picks a home spot and keeps a chest there; surplus goes in; the chest is a place record.
features.acceptance: Personal chests exist with contents.

features.title: Hours of the day
features.what: Work weights shift with the day: gathering by day, crafting and building at dusk, sleep at night.
features.acceptance: Activity mix changes across the day.

features.title: Weather awareness
features.what: In rain people prefer indoor jobs; in thunder they shelter.
features.acceptance: Activity changes with weather.

features.title: Apprenticeship
features.what: A person with skill 0 in a job who works beside someone with skill 3+ gains minutes 50% faster.
features.acceptance: Skill minutes grow faster near a master.

features.title: Aging
features.what: People age a year per N Minecraft days; elders get +1 WIS, -1 STR; at a cap they die of old age (head drops).
features.acceptance: An age field exists and an elder dies naturally.

features.title: Families
features.what: Two people with high regard for each other and a house may have a child NPC (generation+1) born at the house with inherited abilities +-1.
features.acceptance: A child record with parents exists.

features.title: Regard between people
features.what: Each person keeps a regard score per other person, moved by trades, gifts, help and harm; regard shades who they visit and trade with.
features.acceptance: A regard map exists and changes.

features.title: Store accounting
features.what: The store tracks in/out per person; members with the most contribution get first pick at the market.
features.acceptance: A ledger of contributions exists.

features.title: Founding charter
features.what: Founding requires the founder to write a charter (facts: name, rule) which the actor voices when asked.
features.acceptance: A charter fact exists.

features.title: Expansion
features.what: When members exceed beds, the village asks for a second inn or houses; plots are assigned on a grid around the origin.
features.acceptance: A second building is built when population grows.

features.title: Defence
features.what: At night members with swords stand watch at the inn; a placed zombie near the inn is fought.
features.acceptance: A zombie is killed at a village at night.

features.title: Village fields
features.what: Fields near a village are village fields; any member may harvest and the crop goes to the store.
features.acceptance: Store receives wheat from village fields.

features.title: Well
features.what: A village builds a well (cobblestone ring over a water source) as its centre marker.
features.acceptance: A well exists at the origin.

features.title: Gatherings
features.what: Once per day a village with 4+ members holds a gathering at dusk: everyone comes to the inn, social need rises, a rumour is exchanged.
features.acceptance: A gathering event fires.

features.title: Leadership
features.what: The member with the highest reputation is the head; the head assigns the village's build requests.
features.acceptance: A head field exists on the village.

features.title: Taxes
features.what: Members pay one item of value per day into the store; non-payers lose membership after three days.
features.acceptance: Membership changes over unpaid days.

features.title: Trade routes
features.what: Peddlers link villages; a fact records the route; prices equalise over time.
features.acceptance: Two stores show converged prices.

features.title: Animal husbandry
features.what: Animals in pens are fed and bred; babies grow; the pen is the village's meat supply and hunting ranges shrink.
features.acceptance: Pen population grows and hunting frequency drops.

features.title: Hostile nights
features.what: The director places a few hostiles near villages at night on a cadence; guards and walls matter.
features.acceptance: Hostiles appear and are dealt with.

features.title: Lost and found
features.what: Dropped tools are remembered as facts by the dropper and retrieved when passing.
features.acceptance: A dropped tool is picked back up later.

features.title: Boats
features.what: A person with 5 planks crafts a boat and crosses water in it instead of swimming.
features.acceptance: A boat crossing is observed.

features.title: Bridges
features.what: Builders span gaps under 6 blocks with planks on frequently walked routes.
features.acceptance: A bridge exists on a route.

features.title: Signposts
features.what: Villages place signs at their boundary naming the village and pointing to neighbours.
features.acceptance: Signs exist at boundaries.

features.title: Graves
features.what: A dead person's head is buried by a friend under a cobblestone marker with a sign; the grave is a place.
features.acceptance: A grave place exists.

features.title: Head revival ritual
features.what: Bringing a head to a village shrine with 10 food and a bed lets the village revive the person (npc_revive); costs the store.
features.acceptance: A revival happens at a shrine.

features.title: Storm damage
features.what: Plank buildings may lose a block in thunderstorms; builders repair them.
features.acceptance: A repair job runs after a storm.

features.title: Seasons
features.what: Every 20 days a season changes: winter slows crops and raises hunger drain; people stock up in autumn.
features.acceptance: A season field exists and behaviour changes.
